The work requires strong judgment, attention to detail, discretion, and the ability to follow established processes in a high-volume environment. Experience with ACA health insurance enrollment, Healthcare.gov, or state-based marketplaces such as Covered California is strongly preferred. Responsibilities ● Review and process consumer enrollment, termination, and cancellation requests ● Identify and resolve enrollment errors, discrepancies, and missing information ● Follow established processes for handling enrollment activity and sensitive consumer information ● Contact consumers when additional information or action is required ● Research issues and coordinate with internal teams when appropriate ● Escalate complex or high-risk issues with clear documentation ● Maintain accurate records of enrollment activity and communications in Zendesk or similar systems ● Identify recurring issues and communicate trends or process gaps to management ● Support the Enrollment Operations team during periods of high volume Qualifications When reviewing resumes, we'll look for experience that indicates: ● Experience managing detailed, process-driven work in which accuracy and timely execution were essential ● Experience identifying discrepancies, researching issues, and determining or coordinating the appropriate next step ● Experience following established processes and handling sensitive or confidential information ● Experience maintaining accurate records and documenting actions and communications in business systems ● Experience communicating directly with consumers or customers and coordinating with internal teams to resolve issues ● Experience working independently in a high-volume environment with changing priorities ● Experience using technology and digital tools to manage workflows, records, and communications, including learning new systems as needed Preferred Experience We'll prioritize candidates with resumes that indicate: ● Experience in health insurance operations, broker services, member support, or enrollment processing ● Experience with ACA enrollment, including eligibility, plan selection, or coverage changes ● Experience using Healthcare.gov or state-based marketplaces such as Covered California ● Experience using Zendesk or a similar CRM or support platform ● Experience working in a high-volume Open Enrollment environment ● Experience working effectively in a fully remote environment ● Experience in a startup, small business, or similarly fast-paced environment where you were expected to take ownership and wear multiple hats What We'll Assess During the Interview During the interview process, we'll assess: ● Critical thinking and problem-solving - the ability to assess a situation, identify relevant information, and determine the appropriate next step ● Attention to detail - the ability to maintain accuracy under pressure ● Judgment, discretion, and accountability when handling sensitive information and enrollment activity ● Process discipline and independence - the ability to work with limited guidance while following established processes precisely ● Written and verbal communication - the ability to document actions clearly and communicate effectively with consumers and internal teams ● Comfort in a high-volume environment with changing priorities ● Technical learning agility - the ability to learn and navigate new systems quickly ● Ownership and adaptability - the willingness to take responsibility for work and respond effectively to new or unfamiliar tasks What Success Looks Like You process enrollment work accurately, consistently, and on time. You take ownership of your work, recognize when something is wrong, document your actions clearly, and escalate issues appropriately. Accuracy is critical in this role. Small enrollment errors can have significant consequences for consumers, and we expect every team member to treat that responsibility seriously. About Integrity Integrity is one of the nation’s leading independent distributors of life, health and wealth insurance products. With a strong insurtech focus, we embrace a broad and innovative approach to serving agents and clients alike. Integrity is driven by a singular purpose: to help people protect their life, health and wealth so they can prepare for the good days ahead. Integrity offers you the opportunity to start a career in a family-like environment that is rewarding and cutting edge. Why? Because we put our people first! At Integrity, you can start a new career path at company you’ll love, and we’ll love you back. We’re proud of the work we do and the culture we’ve built, where we celebrate your hard work and support you daily. Joining us means being part of a hyper-growth company with tons of professional opportunities for you to accelerate your career. title: Specialist, IT Software Asset Administration (SAM)
jd_text: Title: Specialist, IT Software Asset Administration (SAM) KBR is seeking a Software Asset Management (SAM) Specialist to support the administration, tracking, and compliance of software assets across the organization. This role will assist with software lifecycle processes, maintain accurate asset records, support licensing compliance activities, and collaborate with internal stakeholders to ensure effective software asset management practices. The successful candidate will work closely with IT, Procurement, Finance, and software vendors to support software asset operations, maintain data quality, and contribute to process improvements within the Software Asset Management program. In September 2025, KBR announced that we are spinning our Mission Technology Solutions business into a separate public company. This role will ultimately be part of the new company. The Mission Technology Solutions business partners with governments and defense, intelligence, space, aviation, and critical infrastructure customers to deliver high-end engineering, science, technology, and mission support solutions. Key Responsibilities Support the administration and tracking of software assets throughout their lifecycle, including requests, deployments, renewals, reclamation, and retirement. Maintain accurate records of software licenses, subscriptions, contracts, entitlements, and installations. Assist with software asset management activities using ServiceNow SAM Pro or similar asset management tools. Support software reconciliation, entitlement management, normalization, and reporting processes. Monitor software usage and help identify opportunities for license optimization and cost savings. Assist with software license compliance reviews and support audit readiness activities through data gathering and documentation. Help maintain accurate and audit-ready software asset records in accordance with company policies and procedures. Collaborate with IT, Procurement, Finance, and business teams to support software asset management operations. Support software purchasing, renewal tracking, invoice validation, and contract administration activities. Generate and maintain reports, dashboards, and metrics related to software assets, licensing, and compliance. Assist with resolving software asset and licensing inquiries from internal stakeholders. Support data quality initiatives by validating software inventory, contract, and entitlement information. Contribute to process improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency and data accuracy. Stay current on software licensing and asset management practices and apply established procedures consistently. Basic Qualifications Education & Experience Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 2+ years of experience in Software Asset Management (SAM), IT Asset Management (ITAM), software licensing, IT operations, or a related discipline. Experience working with asset management systems, software inventories, or license tracking processes. Technical Skills Basic understanding of software asset lifecycle management principles. Familiarity with software licensing models, including SaaS and subscription-based licensing. Experience using ServiceNow, ServiceNow SAM Pro, or similar asset management platforms preferred. Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel for reporting and analysis. Strong attention to detail and accuracy in maintaining asset and license records. Good analytical and problem-solving skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting software asset management, license compliance, or IT asset management initiatives. Familiarity with software vendors such as Microsoft, Adobe, Oracle, VMware, or similar enterprise software providers. Working knowledge of procurement, contract administration, or software purchasing processes. Experience supporting software audits and compliance activities. Exposure to cloud software licensing environments, including Microsoft 365, Azure, or AWS. ServiceNow, ITIL, or related IT asset management certifications are a plus. title: Lead Quality Control Technician
jd_text: Classification: Hourly Shift: Second Shift - 8 (United States of America) Job Description: Are you looking for a new challenge? Passionate about innovation? Want to work for a global company that values integrity, teamwork, and loyalty? At LATICRETE International, we aim to be the leading construction brand trusted globally for high-performance tile and stone installation systems and building finishing solutions. We’ve been in business for over 65 years, family-owned for three generations, and can be found in over 100 countries. The Hartford Business Journal even named us one of Connecticut’s top family-owned companies in 2017! We don't just make innovative, industry-leading products. Our purpose is to improve the built world and the lives of those who build it. We strive to connect with, engage with and improve the lives of our employees, our customers, our partners, and the global communities in which we operate. We are seeking passionate and ambitious employees who want to make a difference not just within our organization, but within their communities, our industry, and the world. If that sounds like you, then what are you waiting for? Join the family and expand your horizons! Just some of our benefits: Medical Dental Vision 401k Tuition reimbursement 13 paid holidays, that includes 1 week of paid plant shutdown between the Christmas and New Year's Day holidays Paid vacation and sick time Flexible spending Life Insurance, AD&D and Supplemental Insurance POSITION SUMMARY This position is responsible for providing technical oversight for a local team of in a designated Quality Control lab and ensures that the team meets all the LATICRETE quality criteria. This individual works with the designated Sr. QC Manager and/or Regional Supervisor to oversee the implementation of process improvement initiatives that result in improved processes for Production and implements and supports programs to ensure the Manufacturing Quality Control Team executes efficient, reliable and repeatable Quality Assurance/Control processes and activities. The Quality Control Lead ensures all products manufactured meet or exceed quality standards as well as all safety, environmental and ISO requirements. The Quality Control Lead will provide technical guidance to the local QC team designated by the Sr. QC Manager and/or Regional Supervisor. The QC Lead will ensure that lab’s QC team are accomplishing continuous improvement initiatives in the manufacturing and QC environment. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Additional duties and responsibilities may be assigned as necessary. 1. QC Lab and Process Management (60%): Ensure that (G)ood (L)aboratory (P)ractices are being followed across plants along with 5S methods for laboratory organization and ensures that QC personnel across plants are trained. Lead QC team develop and perform process improvement at local QC lab to meet standard capacity for testing and safety requirements. Be the technical leader with the work process to update and improves QC Lab work instructions, procedures, and calibration of QC instrumentation referenced in the LATICRETE Quality Control Manual. Perform QC tests at the local QC lab. Lead communications between local QC and operations to determine priorities and specific needs to preserve Quality of the product at all the time including the control of non-conforming product. 2. Data Analysis/Technical Management (35%): Work with the Sr. QC Manager or Regional QC Supervisor to ensure that manufacturing and raw material specifications exist and are current and enforced. Perform internal QC lab audits to ensure all QC data is accurate and reliable. Work with Sr. QC Manager/Regional QC Manager, Process Chemist, and Process Engineering team to troubleshoot problems associated with finished product production in assigned facilities. Ensure the local QC team is maintaining a reliable QC database. Report on Quality Metrics Performance for the local manufacturing plant and any potential causes that impact the Quality of the product based on the data provided by the local QC team. 3. Department and People Management (5%): Perform duties of a working QC Lead at homebased QC lab. Develop a rapport with multiple Plant Leadership Teams, QA Team, and R&D personnel. Lead the technical portion of training department employees in QC procedures. Foster a success-oriented, accountable environment, recognizing and rewarding performance that drives desired results. Provide technical leadership to QC team in local lab. Be prepared to travel to other labs as needed. REQUIRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Education and Experience: 7+ years experience working in a lab environment required. Bachelor’s degree (Chemistry or Technical focus desired) or equivalent relevant QC and/or laboratory certifications and experience is a plus. Specialized Skills and Experience : Strong technical knowledge of chemistry in the following area(s): cementitious chemistry, epoxy liquids, latex, and/or any LATICRETE product lines highly preferred. Previous experience with color matching and knowledge or experience utilizing a colorimeter highly desired. Ability to give, receive and analyze information, formulate work plans and prepare written materials and articulate goals and action plans. Ability to do simple math calculations, input data into a computer and analyze data is required. Advanced computer/technical skills including demonstrated experience using Access, ACT, Excel, Word and Strong ERP software knowledge. Able to participate in Quality Control and Environmental Safety Organizations. Able to work independently with minimal oversight. Excellent record keeping, documentation and organizational skills. Able to management multiple assignments and projects simultaneously with shifting priorities, deadlines and focus. Must be adaptable and flexible. Travel Requirement: May be required to travel up 15%. This role will cover designated QC labs. Physical Requirements: Must pass pre-employment physical. Lift: Must be able to lift and/or carry a minimum of 50 pounds repetitively. Occasional lifting of 60+ pounds required. Push/Pull: Must be able to push/pull 50 pounds repetitively. Occasional push/pull of 60+ pounds required. Stand: Must be able to stand 50-75% of the day. Sitting: Must be able to sit 25-50% of the day. Twisting/Bending: Must be able to twist/bend 50-75% of the day. Squatting, Climbing and/or Crawling: Must be able to squat/climb/crawl 20% of the day.

title: Director, Lifecycle Technology & Operations
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><h2 data-pm-slice="1 1 []">About Crunchyroll</h2> <p>Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.</p> <p>Join our team, and help us shape the future of anime!</p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>As the Director, Lifecycle Technology &amp; Operations, you will lead the global operating model and technical foundation that enables Lifecycle Marketing to deliver personalized, data-driven customer experiences at scale.</p> <p>You will oversee global Lifecycle Operations while serving as the primary Lifecycle business owner for our customer engagement and orchestration platform and the broader technology and data ecosystem that powers customer engagement. Today, Braze sits at the center of that ecosystem. You will define platform strategy and stewardship; journey and campaign operations; customer data and audience capabilities; personalization and decisioning; governance; automation; capacity; and partner delivery. This will build capabilities that can scale globally while supporting the needs of individual regions and markets.</p> <p>Sitting at the intersection of Lifecycle Marketing, Marketing Technology, Data, Product, and Operations, this role combines ownership of the technical foundation that powers Lifecycle with leadership of the operating model that brings it to life. You will partner closely with Marketing, Martech, Product, Engineering, Data Engineering, Analytics, and regional teams, serving as the connective tissue among customer strategy, platform capabilities, data, and execution.</p> <p>You will bring strong operational leadership with meaningful technical depth and experience operating at a global scale. You will help build the next stage of Lifecycle Marketing by building a high-performing global operation, shaping the Lifecycle technology roadmap, evolving our customer engagement and orchestration capabilities, diagnosing data and platform issues, and creating processes that enable global strategies to be efficiently localized across markets, languages, channels, and regulatory environments.&nbsp;</p> <h3><strong>Core Areas of Responsibility</strong></h3> <h3><strong>Lifecycle Technology &amp; Platform Leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary Lifecycle business owner and technical subject-matter expert for Braze and the broader Lifecycle technology ecosystem, with deep working knowledge of Braze Canvas and campaign architecture, Liquid, Catalogs, Connected Content and API integrations, segmentation, personalization, experimentation, channel configuration, and AI-enabled decisioning and orchestration capabilities; own platform strategy, governance, configuration standards, roadmap priorities, tooling, consumption, and ongoing platform health.</li> <li>Partner directly with Martech, Product, Engineering, and Data Engineering to define and operationalize the events, attributes, APIs, data contracts, and integrations required to build trigger-based Lifecycle journeys in Braze, including API-based ingestion and utilization of content and metadata to power real-time, contextually relevant intervention messaging across global and regional teams.</li> <li>Serve as Lifecycle’s dedicated partner to the Braze Technical Account team, leading enhancement discovery, technical recommendations, platform adoption, and roadmap planning; translate emerging Braze and AI capabilities into prioritized use cases and regularly share roadmap implications, recommendations, and enablement guidance with cross-functional Lifecycle Directors and Leadership.</li> <li>Establish best practices for journey architecture, event-driven messaging, segmentation, channel orchestration, experimentation, personalization, and reusable platform capabilities.</li> <li>Maintain a strong understanding of how our customer engagement and orchestration platform connects to Product, customer data platforms, content systems, analytics, reporting, and downstream destinations, and identify opportunities to improve or simplify the ecosystem.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Global Lifecycle Operations</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Lead the global operating model supporting Lifecycle teams and programs across regions and markets, including subscription journeys and automations, regional marketing, ecommerce, games, manga, theatrical, events, and the broader Crunchyroll fan ecosystem.</li> <li>Own the end-to-end operational process from intake and prioritization through audience development, campaign and journey build, QA, deployment, monitoring, and optimization.</li> <li>Build scalable campaign and journey operations that allow global strategies and capabilities to be efficiently adapted and localized across markets, languages, channels, and regulatory requirements while maintaining speed, quality, and consistency.</li> <li>Build and continuously improve a flexible delivery model across internal teams, regional resources, agency partners, offshore resources, specialized technical expertise, and automation.</li> <li>Establish clear standards for prioritization, capacity management, development, QA, launch readiness, documentation, incident management, and operational performance—continually improving speed, quality, reliability, and efficiency.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Lifecycle Data, Audiences &amp; Personalization</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Own Lifecycle Marketing requirements for the events, attributes, audiences, preferences, behavioral signals, content data, and other customer inputs needed to power personalized experiences across markets.</li> <li>Partner with CDI, Data Engineering, Martech, Product, and Analytics to identify data gaps, improve signal quality and observability, and prioritize instrumentation and integration needs.</li> <li>Enable increasingly sophisticated audience creation, behavioral triggers, content affinity, personalization, decisioning, and next-best-action capabilities that can be applied globally while allowing for regional and market-level relevance.</li> <li>Translate customer and marketing strategies into clear data and technical requirements and help ensure Lifecycle-critical data is reliable, measurable, and fit for purpose.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Governance, Automation &amp; Scale</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Reimagine and maintain global governance for customer communications, including messaging hierarchy, prioritization, frequency management, consent and preferences, suppression logic, and cross-channel coordination.</li> <li>Define scalable global standards for campaign quality, approvals, deliverability, accessibility, localization readiness, documentation, and operational controls, while accommodating market-specific requirements where needed.</li> <li>Identify and implement practical applications of automation and AI across audience creation, journey development, QA, personalization, content production, workflow management, reporting, and knowledge management.</li> <li>Continuously evaluate new platform capabilities and emerging technologies, helping move high-value opportunities from pilots into repeatable, scalable solutions across markets.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Team &amp; Cross-Functional Leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Build, develop, and lead a high-performing Lifecycle Technology &amp; Operations team with strong capabilities across platform enablement, journey development, campaign operations, data quality, and operational governance.</li> <li>Manage agency and external partner performance across quality, throughput, cost, technical capability, service levels, and continuous improvement, building partners toward greater autonomy and accountability.</li> <li>Serve as a key connector between global Lifecycle Marketing, regional teams, and technical partners, translating marketing ambition into technical requirements while helping marketers understand platform capabilities, constraints, and opportunities.</li> <li>Influence cross-functional technology and data roadmaps by clearly articulating Lifecycle use cases, customer impact, regional requirements, dependencies, operational needs, and measurable business value.</li> </ul> <p>In the role of Director, Lifecycle Technology &amp; Operations, you will report to the VP, Lifecycle Marketing.</p> <p>We are considering applicants for the locations of Los Angeles or Dallas.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>About You</strong></h2> <p>We get excited about candidates, like you, because...</p> <ul> <li>12+ years of experience across Lifecycle Marketing Operations, CRM Operations, Marketing Technology, Marketing Operations, customer engagement platforms, or related disciplines within a scaled consumer business.</li> <li>5+ years of experience leading teams, complex marketing operations, or technical marketing programs, including management of internal and external resources.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience leading Lifecycle, CRM, Martech, or marketing operations across multiple regions and markets, including building global capabilities that support localization, regional requirements, and market-specific execution.</li> <li>Deep experience with Braze ESP, including journey orchestration, segmentation, behavioral triggers, personalization, experimentation, and multi-channel execution.</li> <li>Technical understanding of JavaScript and HTML, with the ability to use both to configure and support lifecycle marketing-platform experiences and integrations.</li> <li>Hands-on experience setting up, managing, and troubleshooting data connections in Databricks to support reliable data pipelines, integrations, audience activation, and downstream marketing-platform use cases.</li> <li>Strong technical fluency across customer data architecture, events, attributes, audiences, APIs, integrations, data pipelines, identity, and data-quality monitoring.</li> <li>Experience serving as a platform owner, senior business stakeholder, or highly technical operator responsible for how a customer engagement or marketing automation platform is configured, governed, used, and evolved.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to translate customer and marketing needs into technical requirements, platform capabilities, roadmaps, and scalable solutions.</li> <li>Experience partnering closely with MarTech, Product, Engineering, Data Engineering, Analytics, Marketing, and regional teams to deliver new customer-facing and operational capabilities.</li> <li>Experience supporting global localization across markets.</li> <li>Proven experience designing and improving global operating models, including intake, prioritization, resource and capacity management, QA, governance, deployment, and incident management.</li> <li>Experience managing agencies, offshore teams, vendors, budgets, and technology or platform investments.</li> <li>Strong understanding of customer-contact governance, deliverability, suppression logic, consent and preference management, privacy, and operational risk across complex markets.</li> <li>Demonstrated success advancing personalization, automation, experimentation, decisioning, or real-time customer engagement capabilities.</li> <li>Ability to move comfortably between marketing, operational, data, and technical conversations and translate complex concepts for different audiences.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional leadership, influencing, program management, and problem-solving skills within complex, matrixed, global organizations.</li> <li>Experience within streaming, subscription, entertainment, gaming, ecommerce, media, or another high-volume digital consumer business is strongly preferred.</li> <li>Experience applying AI or emerging marketing technologies to improve scale, efficiency, or customer experience is strongly preferred.</li> <li>Passion for anime, entertainment, or fandom-driven businesses is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>Lifecycle Marketing is part of Crunchyroll’s broader Growth organization and is responsible for building deeper, more relevant relationships with fans throughout their journey with Crunchyroll.</p> <p>Our team works globally across membership engagement and retention, regional title marketing, ecommerce, games, manga, theatrical, events, and other parts of the Crunchyroll fan experience. We partner closely with Product, Martech, Data, Analytics, Content, and regional teams to connect those experiences through increasingly personalized, data-driven customer communications.</p> <p>Lifecycle Technology &amp; Operations provides the operational and technical foundation that makes that work scalable, reliable, locally relevant, and increasingly sophisticated across global markets.</p> <h2><strong>Why you will love working at Crunchyroll</strong></h2> <p>In addition to getting to work with fun, passionate and inspired colleagues, you will also enjoy the following benefits and perks:</p> <ul> <li>Receive a great compensation package including salary plus performance bonus earning potential, paid annually.</li> <li>Flexible time off policies allowing you to take the time you need to be your whole self.</li> <li>Generous medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance</li> <li>Health Saving Account HSA program</li> <li>Health care and dependent care FSA</li> <li>401(k) plan, with employer match</li> <li>Employer paid commuter benefit</li> <li>Support program for new parents</li> <li>Pet insurance and some of our offices are pet friendly!</li> </ul> <p>#LifeAtCrunchyroll #LI-Hybrid</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h3 data-pm-slice="1 1 []">About our Values</h3> <p>We want to be everything for someone rather than something for everyone and we do this by living and modeling our values in all that we do. We value</p> <ul> <li> <p>Courage. We believe that when we overcome fear, we enable our best selves.</p> </li> <li> <p>Curiosity. We are curious, which is the gateway to empathy, inclusion, and understanding.</p> </li> <li>Kaizen. We have a growth mindset committed to constant forward progress.</li> <li> <p>Service. We serve our community with humility, enabling joy and belonging for others.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Our commitment to diversity and inclusion</h3> <p>Our mission of helping people belong reflects our commitment to diversity &amp; inclusion. It's just the way we do business.</p> <p>We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Crunchyroll. Pursuant to applicable law, we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.</p> <p>Crunchyroll, LLC is an independently operated joint venture between US-based Sony Pictures Entertainment, and Japan's Aniplex, a subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc., both subsidiaries of Tokyo-based Sony Group Corporation.</p> <p><em data-stringify-type="italic">Questions about Crunchyroll’s hiring process? title: Business Planning Manager – Chief of Staff
location: Spring, Texas, United States of America
jd_text: Business Planning Manager – Chief of Staff Description - This Business Planning Manager – Chief of Staff is responsible for driving the company's strategic direction, ensuring that it remains competitive and adaptable in a rapidly changing business landscape. The role develops strategic recommendations by overseeing synthesis of data, conduction of in-depth analysis, and rigorous testing of hypotheses, ensuring well-informed strategic choices. The role works with large, cross-functional teams to facilitate projects and collaborates across businesses to align strategy with organizational goals. Responsibilities Identifies research, tools, and analysis required to achieve objectives for large, complex business strategy projects. Structures analytical approaches and develops project strategies and tactics. Develops recommendations for optimizing business and financial performance. Manages large, cross-functional teams and communications to facilitate projects and ensure timely delivery to clients. Leads the development of project guidelines, contingency plans, objectives, and deliverables to drive successful outcomes. Consults with business executives on a wide range of issues related to the strategy formulation process, including risk management and new growth opportunities. Provides thought leadership and contributes to expanding the knowledge base within area of expertise which includes developing new methods, techniques and criteria for developing strategy analysis and recommendations. Collaborates across businesses, functions, and regions to align strategy and direction with corporate and divisional approaches, systems, information and support. Leverages strategic and management consulting frameworks to implement a comprehensive portfolio approach for evaluating and managing the organization's diverse business units, platforms, and products. Facilitates regular follow-ups on strategic planning to foster collaboration and ensure accountability. title: Distinguished Technologist - Principal Architect, Platform Security and Firmware Systems
location: Spring, Texas, United States of America
jd_text: Distinguished Technologist - Principal Architect, Platform Security and Firmware Systems Description - HP is seeking a senior technical leader to serve as a lead architect for hardware rooted Platform Root of Trust for HP's commercial PC platform. In this role, you will be responsible for envisioning, defining, and driving the architecture of hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-integrated security capabilities that protect HP commercial PCs from current and emerging threats. You will also work across the hardware and security architecture teams, collaborate with HP's Security Research Labs, Firmware (BIOS) team, our security business that creates and deploys industry leading enterprise security and manageability solutions, product management, manufacturing, supply chain, customer enablement, and field organizations to create cohesive system solutions that deliver unique customer value. This position requires deep expertise in embedded systems, platform firmware, hardware, security, device manageability, and PC system architecture. The role also requires the ability to translate complex technical capabilities into customer-relevant value propositions and to influence internal and external stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority. Responsibilities Serve as principal architect for HP Endpoint Security Controller roadmap, associated hardware and firmware based capabilities, cryptographic identity, attestation, secure communication, event logging, and future controller generations. Define and evolve HP Sure Start architecture and related firmware resilience capabilities, including hardware-enforced firmware authenticity, recovery, update, and protection mechanisms. Drive secure BIOS and firmware configuration management strategies, including HP Sure Admin ecosystem capabilities, key management, zero-touch provisioning, customer deployment models, and integration with enterprise management tools. Lead cross-functional architecture definition across hardware, BIOS, embedded controller firmware, diagnostics, cloud services, client software, manageability tools, product management, and customer-facing teams. Anticipate emerging threats and technology shifts, including quantum-safe cryptography, platform attestation, supply-chain security, physical tamper resistance, peripheral authentication, and new non-volatile memory architectures. Partner with silicon vendors, operating-system providers, standards organizations, internal and external security research teams, and internal product teams to influence and align platform security direction. Support customer briefings, field escalations, competitive positioning, technical marketing, training events, and executive communications related to HP commercial PC platform security. Create specifications, proof-of-concepts, validation tools, scripts, demonstrations, and reference implementations that accelerate adoption of new security capabilities. Mentor engineers and technical leaders by sharing architectural context, reviewing designs, developing talent, and helping teams make practical tradeoffs among security, cost, schedule, customer experience, and portfolio impact. Education & Experience Recommended Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience. Extensive experience in PC, embedded, firmware, hardware, or platform system architecture, preferably in commercial client systems or security-sensitive devices. Demonstrated ability to architect solutions that span hardware, firmware, software, cloud services, manufacturing, and customer deployment environments. Deep technical understanding of BIOS/UEFI, embedded controllers, secure boot, firmware update and recovery flows, cryptographic signing, PKI based device identity, attestation, and secure configuration management. Experience defining product requirements, writing technical specifications, driving proof-of-concepts, and influencing roadmap decisions across multiple engineering teams. Ability to communicate complex technical ideas clearly to executive, engineering, customer, sales, and field audiences. Proven ability to lead through influence in a matrixed organization and to resolve ambiguity across competing business, technical, and customer priorities. Preferred Qualifications Experience with hardware based roots of trust, platform certificates, DICE/SPDM concepts, supply-chain assurance, quantum-safe cryptography, secure element or embedded security controller identity, and compliance or certification frameworks. Experience with enterprise endpoint manageability platforms such as Intune, SCCM, device-management consoles, or cloud-based key management services. Hands-on capability with scripting or development tools such as PowerShell, C#, Python, Java, GitHub, Visual Studio Code, or similar environments. Experience with customer-facing technical briefings, sales enablement, competitive analysis, standards participation, patent development, or external security ecosystem collaboration. Familiarity with commercial PC platform architecture, silicon vendor security technologies, Windows platform security, docking, peripheral security, battery authentication, telemetry, and right-to-repair considerations. Critical Technical Domains HP Endpoint Security Controller architecture, roadmap definition, cryptographic identity, attestation evidence, enhanced logging, and next-generation hardware requirements. HP Sure Start and firmware resilience, including hardware-enforced firmware authenticity, recovery, update protection, and quantum-safe firmware protection. HP Sure Admin and secure BIOS settings management, including key management, zero-touch provisioning, smart card or YubiKey authentication concepts, fine-grained authorization, and enterprise deployment workflows. Platform security roadmap planning across BIOS, embedded controller firmware, manufacturing diagnostics, endpoint management tools, and customer-facing security capabilities. Future-looking architecture areas such as target-attached flash, SPI-NAND, secure NV storage, peripheral authentication, SPDM requester/responder models, DICE-style identity, and post-quantum cryptography retrofits. Leadership Expectations Operate as a senior individual contributor who sets technical direction, creates architectural clarity, and helps HP prioritize the highest-value security investments. Build trust with cross-functional engineering teams by understanding implementation detail while keeping focus on the larger system architecture and customer outcome. Help convert exploratory concepts into practical product plans, proof-of-concepts, specifications, and production-ready capabilities. Represent HP platform security credibly in customer, partner, industry, and internal executive discussions. Develop and mentor technical talent so the organization can scale architectural knowledge and continue delivering differentiated security innovation. Measures of Success Clear, actionable architecture and roadmap for next-generation HP platform security capabilities. Successful delivery of security-controller, firmware-resilience, secure-management, and attestation capabilities into commercial PC products. Increased adoption of HP security capabilities by enterprise customers and improved ability for field teams to explain HP’s differentiated platform security value. Reduced ambiguity and improved prioritization across security-related product planning, engineering execution, and customer enablement efforts. Growth of technical bench strength through mentoring, documentation, design reviews, and knowledge transfer. jd_text: Principal Enterprise Architect Description - Position Overview The Principal Enterprise Architect plays a strategic architecture role within the Office of the CIO. The role helps establish and mature an enterprise architecture capability that connects business priorities with technology strategy and execution across the HP Enterprise. The Principal Enterprise Architect translates business strategy into target architectures, transition roadmaps, standards, and investment guidance across business, application, data, integration, cloud, technology, and AI domains. The role promotes reuse and simplification and helps teams deliver secure, scalable, resilient, and business-aligned solutions. Key Responsibilities Help define and operationalize the enterprise architecture operating model, principles, methods, standards, decision rights, and measures of value. Lead architecture for major enterprise initiatives from strategy and discovery through target-state definition, transition planning, and delivery guidance. Develop current-state assessments, target architectures, reference architectures, and multiyear roadmaps for critical enterprise capabilities and platforms. Connect business strategy, operating models, and capability needs to technology priorities, portfolio choices, and investment decisions. Guide simplification, reuse, interoperability, application rationalization, lifecycle management, and technical debt reduction across a complex global technology landscape. Assess complex technology choices and recommend patterns, platforms, and strategic direction based on business value, total cost, scalability, resilience, interoperability, and long-term fit. Define and maintain reusable architecture assets, including principles, standards, reference architectures, patterns, and decision records. title: Principal, Enterprise Applications Engineering Lead
jd_text: Position Overview: We are seeking a highly technical and strategic Principal Engineering Lead to lead the engineering organization responsible for our Enterprise Applications portfolio. This individual will serve as the technical leader for a team supporting Salesforce, DealCloud, DevOps, and Quality Engineering while partnering closely with Product Specialists and Functional Architecture to deliver scalable, AI-enabled business solutions. This is a hands-on player-coach role, not a traditional people management position. The successful candidate is expected to actively participate in architecture, solution design, proof-of-concepts, code reviews, and complex technical problem solving while leading and developing a high-performing engineering organization. Approximately 40–50% of the role will remain hands-on technical work, with the remainder focused on engineering leadership, mentoring, delivery, and cross-functional collaboration. What you'll do: Set and own the technical direction for enterprise applications — leading architecture reviews, solution design, and proof-of-concepts across Salesforce, Intapp DealCloud, and related platforms while staying close enough to the work to remove blockers and solve the hardest problems alongside your team. Define engineering standards, coding guidelines, and development best practices, and hold the organization to them — including CI/CD, automated testing, DevSecOps, observability, and a production support model with clear SLAs and root cause accountability. Champion AI-assisted development as a daily practice, lead proof-of-concepts for emerging technologies, and build reusable frameworks that accelerate delivery across the portfolio. Partner with product specialists and functional architects during discovery to translate business requirements into scalable, secure, and maintainable technical solutions — and provide technical leadership across the organization's most complex cross-functional initiatives. Coach and develop engineers at every level through active involvement in their technical growth, manage capacity across concurrent initiatives, and build a team culture defined by ownership, continuous improvement, and engineering excellence. What you'll need: Proven experience as a senior technical leader in a complex enterprise applications environment, with a track record of setting architecture direction and staying hands-on in delivery — not just managing people. Deep Salesforce development experience, including platform architecture, integrations, and customizations; familiarity with Intapp DealCloud or a comparable CRM platform is a plus. Strong DevOps foundations: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, release management, observability tooling, and a working knowledge of DevSecOps practices. Experience integrating AI tooling into engineering workflows and a genuine interest in pushing further — this team is expected to lead by example on AI-assisted development. The communication range to work across audiences — as comfortable driving an architecture decision with senior engineers as explaining a technical trade-off to a business leader. What you will gain: At Intapp, you’ll get the opportunity to bring your talents and intellectual curiosity to create better outcomes for our people and our clients. You’ll be part of a growing public company, with a modern work environment that’s connected yet flexible and where your professional growth and well-being are top priorities. We’ll collaborate and grow together, supporting each other in a positive, open atmosphere that fosters creativity, innovation, and teamwork. We offer reimbursement for training and continuing education to help you stay ahead in your career. Enjoy Where You Work: Thrive in our modern, open offices designed to inspire creativity and collaboration. Our complimentary lunches and fully stocked kitchens ensure you have everything you need to stay energized throughout the day. title: Director of Security Operations, Programs
jd_text: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,300 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve . The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, w e are seeking a Director of Security Operations to serve as the principal security partner to IJM's program leadership, ensuring security considerations are embedded into program design, operational planning, survivor engagement strategies, investigative operations, and geographic expansion initiatives from the outset. This role operates from a clear mission-enabling posture. IJM's work is hard, and at times dangerous. The organization maintains a high tolerance for measured risk because the mission often requires operating in places and circumstances that other organizations may avoid. The Director of Security Operations is not a gatekeeper whose default posture is to stop or delay programs. Rather, this leader exists to help programs keep moving forward by shaping safe, practical, and risk-informed ways of operating in complex environments. Working in close partnership with program leadership, the Director identifies emerging threats, anticipates future operational requirements, and develops security frameworks that support program growth, innovation, and operational effectiveness. By maintaining early visibility into evolving casework models, survivor engagement strategies, office expansions, and new operational initiatives, the Director ensures security considerations are integrated proactively rather than applied retroactively. Success in this role is measured not by the avoidance of risk, but by the ability to help programs achieve their objectives safely, responsibly, and without unnecessary operational delay. The Director of Security Operations serves as a trusted advisor, strategic partner, and problem solver who balances mission objectives with the safety of staff, survivors, witnesses, partners, and the organization. All of this is done with a standard of excellence. This position is hybrid (onsite Tuesdays & Thursdays) if located in the Washington, DC area or remote for non-local candidates. It reports to the Vice President, Safety and Security and is only available for candidates with the right to work in the US. Responsibilities: Leadership & Management Provide strategic leadership for IJM's global Program Security function, ensuring security is fully integrated into program planning and operations and serves as a critical enabler of mission success in IJM complex program environments; Serve as a trusted advisor to senior program leaders and contribute to organizational strategy, risk management, and decision-making processes; Foster a culture of mission-enabling security, accountability, collaboration, spiritual health, and operational excellence; Lead, supervise, coach, and develop Program Security personnel as assigned; Provide security leadership during crises, critical incidents, and other high-risk operational situations affecting programs, staff, survivors, and partners; Strategy, Knowledge Development & Implementation Partner with program leadership to integrate security considerations into new program models, strategic initiatives, office expansions, and operational planning; Provide early analysis of emerging programmatic risks and opportunities to support informed decision-making; Develop and implement program security frameworks, standards, and solutions that enable programs to operate effectively in challenging environments; Maintain visibility into future program direction and operational changes to proactively prepare security capabilities and infrastructure; Contribute subject matter expertise to organizational planning, policy development, and implementation of IJM's Theory of Change; Networking & Partnership Develop and maintain strategic relationships with global and regional program leaders, survivor services leaders, legal teams, investigations teams, and operational stakeholders; Serve as the primary security point of contact for assigned programs and initiatives; Collaborate with Regional Security Directors to ensure alignment between program priorities and regional security support; Represent the Global Safety & Security Team in cross-functional planning forums, working groups, and organizational initiatives; Policies & Procedures Develop, review, and maintain program security policies, standards, protocols, and operational guidance; Ensure security considerations are incorporated into program design processes, operational planning frameworks, and organizational procedures; Recommend improvements to security governance, risk management processes, and operational standards based on emerging threats and lessons learned; Support the implementation and continuous improvement of the Field Security Operations Manual and related guidance documents ; Communication Communicate security risks, mitigation measures, and operational recommendations clearly to program and organizational leadership; Prepare security briefings, assessments, decision-support documents, and executive updates related to program operations; Facilitate rapid communication and decision-making during incidents, crises, and high-risk operational activities; Promote a shared understanding of risk tolerance and mission-enabling security throughout the organization; Training & Development Develop and deliver training, workshops, and briefings to strengthen security awareness and risk management capabilities across program teams; Provide coaching and informal mentoring to program leaders on security planning and operational risk management; Support organizational capacity-building initiatives related to staff safety, survivor protection, and program security practices; Research, Program Management & M&E Conduct security risk assessments and operational reviews for new initiatives, office expansions, investigations, survivor services activities, and other program operations; Monitor security trends, emerging threats, and operational risks that may impact program effectiveness; Evaluate the effectiveness of security measures and recommend adjustments to support program objectives ; Support after-action reviews, lessons learned processes, and continuous improvement initiatives following significant incidents or operational activities; and Participation in IJM’s community of spiritual formation . Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Security Management , Criminal Justice, International Relations, Risk Management, Emergency Management, Law Enforcement, Military Studies, or a related field; Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in security, risk management, humanitarian operations, law enforcement, military service, international development, or a related field; Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience managing complex security operations or risk programs; Demonstrated experience conducting security risk assessments and developing mitigation strategies in high-risk environments; Experience supporting investigations, legal operations, survivor-centered programming, or other sensitive operational activities; Experience working in international or cross-cultural settings; Demonstrated expertise in program security risk management, security risk assessment, and mitigation planning; Experience supporting program operations, survivor protection, field security, and duty of care initiatives; Experience providing strategic security advice and executive-level risk communication; Experience designing and delivering security training and capacity-building programs; Experience developing security policies, governance structures, and operational frameworks; Demonstrated capability in crisis management, incident response, and business continuity planning; Experience conducting intelligence analysis and threat assessments to support operational decision-making; Ability to lead across functions and coordinate effectively within complex, matrixed stakeholder environments; Experience leveraging security technology and travel risk management systems to support organizational objectives ; Advanced degree in a related field; Professional certifications such as CPP, PSP, PCI, CSMP, ISO 31000 Risk Management, or equivalent; Experience supporting anti-trafficking, human rights, rule of law, child protection, or humanitarian organizations; Experience working across multiple geographic regions and complex stakeholder environments; and Mature orthodox Christian faith as defined by the Apostles' Creed. C ritical Qualities: Eager commitment to IJM's Core Values: Christian, Professional and Bridge-Building; Strategic thinking and foresight; Ability to influence without formal authority; Mission-enabling mindset; Sound judgment and decision-making; Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills; Executive presence and credibility; Excellent communication and facilitation skills; Adaptability and organizational agility; Emotional intelligence and situational awareness; Integrity and stewardship; Self-starter with strong initiative; Ability to navigate ambiguity and complexity with confidence; and Commitment to excellence in service of IJM's mission. Application Process: Upload Resume, Cover Letter & Statement of Faith* in one PDF document . *What is a statement of faith? A statement of faith should describe your Christian faith and how you see it as relevant to your involvement with IJM. The statement can either be incorporated into the cover letter or submitted as a separate document and should include, at a minimum, a description of your spiritual disciplines (prayer, study, etc.) and your current fellowship or place of worship. What does IJM have to offer? Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision benefits Monthly commuter and parking benefits in the DC metro area Retirement benefit options Paid leave starting at 23 days 12 holidays (plus early release the day prior) Daily, quarterly, and annual community spiritual formation Robust staff care resources IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidates value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes. At IJM, we’re committed to building a diverse workforce through fair and equitable employment practices. IJM encourages people of any race, color, age, sex, marital status or political ideology to apply for employment. While we welcome everyone into this work, we truly believe that the work we are doing is God’s work, not our own, and practice spiritual disciplines together daily. That’s why we legally require under SEC. 2000e-1 [Section702] of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 that all employees practice a mature orthodox Christian faith, as defined by the Apostles’ Creed. I JM requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.

title: US Procurement Manager
jd_text: Company: INEOS Oxide Interested in joining a winning team? A team whose employees share in the ownership of the business and are empowered to make a difference? COMPENSATION NOTE: Indicative grade - Hay 37/S1, subject to job grade evaluation and candidate level of experience. Role Organizational Context and Job Purpose INEOS Organization : INEOS is a global manufacturer of petrochemicals, specialty chemicals and oil products. It comprises 15 businesses each with a major chemical company heritage. Its production network spans 65 manufacturing facilities in 16 countries throughout the world. INEOS products make a significant contribution to saving life, improving health and enhancing standards of living for people around the world. Its businesses produce the raw materials that are essential in the manufacture of a wide variety of goods: from paints to plastics, textiles to technology, and medicines to mobile phones - chemicals manufactured by INEOS enhance almost every aspect of modern life. BUSINESS CONTEXT: Ethylene oxide (EO) is an important building block for the preparation of a wide variety of EO derivatives (EODs), including various surfactants, as well as a host of other chemical intermediates including Glycol Ethers, Polyethlene Glycols, Ethanolamines, and Alkyl Alkanolamines. INEOS Oxide is one of the world’s leading producers of Ethylene Oxide (EO) and Ethylene Oxide Derivatives (EODs). We currently have a total EO and EOD capacity of 920 kta spread across five different production units throughout Europe and the US. These units have leading cost economics, due to economies of scale, state-of-the-art technology, strategic locations, etc. Our EO project in the US is targeting the fast-growing merchant EO market, building on our experience and leadership position in Europe. Purpose of the Job: The U.S Procurement Manager manages and coordinates Oxide’s U.S. Procurement team’s activities. The incumbent is expected to ensure that raw materials, technical materials, plant services, and logistics are safely and reliably secured at the lowest-possible cost, guaranteeing uninterrupted operations and superior customer service. The position requires a thorough understanding of contract law and what value the terms and conditions hold in a contract negotiation. These legal concepts include seller indemnifications, limitations of liability, warranties and guarantees (length and monetary value) and legal remedies. Most Important Internal Factors: Executing this role’s wide-ranging remit at both a tactical and strategic level will require the post-holder to interface directly with, and influence, the organisation far beyond their immediate procurement team. Board – reporting performance and agreeing procurement strategy and DOAs. Business and Product Managers – providing business and margin environment; how procurement can help lift results and improve the customer’s experience. Site Operations – understand requirements, monitor vendor performance, and provide commercial support when performance issues arise, support CFC and CAPEX target delivery. Procurement INEOS Oxide Europe and other INEOS divisions – network, share and look at leverage opportunities Most Important Internal Factors: Executing this role effectively will require a similarly wide-ranging engagement with parties in the external market: Suppliers – seek offers, launch RFQs, negotiate and align vendor deliverables with INEOS standards, pursue strategic partnership opportunities. Strong industry contacts, executive levels of major suppliers. Consultants/Market info – monitor market activities, trends and prices. RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES Highest level of customer service/satisfaction at the lowest possible cost via: Accountability 1: SHE Most important activities: This position – and all positions – with the INEOS Oxide organization - requires that the incumbent commit to learning, following, and practicing INEOS’ 20 Principles of Process & Behavioural Safety as applicable to the position. These Principles are posted throughout each Oxide facility. The incumbent must also commit to following INEOS’ Life-Saving rules on a daily basis. These are also posted within each Oxide facility. Ensure the procurement team’s activities comply with industry regulations, SHE requirements, hazardous materials rules, and internal governance. This includes supplier risk assessments, documentation control, and ensuring all suppliers meet safety, quality, regulatory, environmental, and SCOC standards. Accountability 2: Organization/Team Management Most important activities: Organize, lead & coach an efficient procurement team – control spend and costs. Set clear KPIs. Establish goals that provide direction and priorities on both tactical and strategic activities for direct reports that support the operational and business objectives and monitor progress towards their realization. Champion a culture where individuals are empowered to achieve and exceed, by delivering solutions that create value in the most innovative, efficient, and cost-conscious way possible. Recognize and reward achievement. Mentor and develop direct reports’ capabilities and build their category expertise; elevate the team’s analytical rigor and negotiation skill. Evaluate individual performance relative to goals. Strive for efficiency in procedures and working practices, drive continuous improvement. Recruitment of staff with required skill level. Network with other INEOS companies to improve efficiency/cost. Accountability 3: Develop and deliver procurement strategies Most important activities: Set sourcing strategy for all categories and guide negotiations that ensure delivery at lowest-possible cost on terms most favourable to Oxide; develop alternate sources and reduce single point vulnerabilities. Guide periodic market reviews, benchmarking, and renegotiation to help protect margins in volatile chemical markets. Coordinate with the businesses, operations, maintenance, and supply chain to anticipate needs and demand; ensuring raw materials, critical spares, materials and contracted services arrive on time; and preventing stockouts, reduced production levels or unplanned downtime. Accountability 4: Delegation of Authority Most important activities: Ensure that DOA is followed at all times. Accountability 5: Assist in or direct contract negotiations, review contract language. Oversee the development, negotiation, and administration of supplier contracts across all categories. Ensure adherence to company procurement policies, legal standards, regulatory requirements, and ethical sourcing practices across the team Manage contractual activity and timelines, guide contract negotiations and terms towards those most favourable for INEOS Oxide. Review contract language in detail, particularly indemnification, liability, insurance, and warranties. Ensure that contracts are developed to an execution-ready state. Skills/Competencies Level of Education & Experience in general 15+ years of front-line procurement experience within the chemical industry. Supervisory skills. Profound knowledge of Procurement and Procurement Management. Experience of leading teams in a diverse working environment. Degree in engineering preferred, or other master's degree. Fluency in English essential. Technical Skills Commercial acumen, deep understanding of cost drivers in contracts. Advanced negotiation skills. Advanced analytical and economic analysis skills. Good understanding of SHE aspects in relation to production and distribution of chemicals. Understanding of chemical manufacturing processes and practices. Knowledge of contract law and ABC regulations. Knowledge of business accounting principles and practice. Fluent in KPI tracking. Ability to work with MS-Office and SAP tools efficiently and effectively. Behavioral Skills Decisive and tenacious in pursuit of objectives, demonstrating a proactive mentality and bias for action. Leadership – inspire and motivate others, sell ideas internally and externally, negotiate, build team spirit. Perspicacious nature – commercially astute, strong intellect, adept at innovative, analytical, tactical and strategic thought. Highly numerate with an analytical mind-set, and attentive to detail. Calm under pressure, able to make quick, clear and reasoned decisions in a dynamic environment. Leader of people, effective at engaging others in working together towards a common goal. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, natural relationship builder. Exert up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication and to make discriminations in sound. This job is performed mainly in a temperature-controlled office environment. title: Compliance Analyst, Audit Assurance
jd_text: Position Summary The Audit & Assurance Analyst supports the Enterprise Compliance and Risk team in executing risk-based assurance activities across the organization's control environment. The role executes the external audit program for the certified business units, covering System and Organization Controls and HITRUST engagements and agreed-upon procedures, and supports internal assurance over the risk framework without assuming direct management responsibility for the processes reviewed. The function is consolidating a fragmented external audit estate onto a single firm and a single platform, so this role participates in a genuine transformation rather than maintaining a steady state. The ideal candidate brings a foundational understanding of insurance operations, risk management principles, and audit methodology, with strong analytical and communication skills. It suits someone detail-oriented, comfortable working across functions, and looking to grow within a maturing and high-visibility program. Key Responsibilities Execute System and Organization Controls and HITRUST readiness activities, including evidence collection, control walkthroughs, and gap identification Support external audit fieldwork and manage auditor requests through to closure within agreed timeframes Maintain audit-ready control evidence within the enterprise GRC platform to support ongoing assurance activity Conduct independent assessments to determine whether major business risks are accurately identified, evaluated, and reported by management Support consistent application of risk appetite and tolerance policies across the organization as those standards are established Track and validate closure of issues and corrective actions taken by management to address identified risk or control gaps Support the findings process, including tracking, validation, and reporting of finding status and remediation progress Identify trends and systemic issues emerging from findings data to inform risk prioritization Support information technology general control testing in coordination with Finance and Internal Audit Assist in preparing documentation for audits, regulatory reviews, and internal assessments Support the consolidation of external audit engagements onto a single firm, including transition of evidence and working papers Partner with compliance, risk, legal, technology, and business unit teams to drive process standardization Support communication of assurance findings to stakeholders with varying levels of risk expertise Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Business, or a related field 1 to 3 years of experience in information technology audit, internal audit, assurance, or control testing; title: Procurement Process Manager
jd_text: About the Role Integrity's Procure-to-Pay (P2P) function is a critical enabler of operational efficiency, financial control, and scalable growth. Our P2P organization is focused on delivering standardized, connected, and optimized processes across procurement and payables while driving a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence. As a Procurement Process Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring all components of the Procure-to-Pay lifecycle are fully integrated, aligned, and operating efficiently. This role has a strong emphasis on operations, execution discipline, and driving efficiency across the end-to-end P2P process. You will act as a process leader and change agent, ensuring that P2P operations are streamlined, scalable, compliant, and well understood across the organization. Success in this role will depend heavily on strong stakeholder management, enabling alignment, adoption, and accountability across diverse business partners. Who We Are Looking For We are seeking a highly collaborative, operations-focused professional who thrives in driving efficiency and improving process execution in a complex, cross-functional environment. The ideal candidate will bring deep understanding of end-to-end P2P operations and the ability to enhance performance through process discipline, data insights, and stakeholder engagement. This role requires someone who can translate operational challenges into actionable improvements, proactively identify gaps (including off-channel spend), and partner effectively across teams to drive adoption and compliance. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated ability to identify and capture value from supplier relationships—going beyond cost savings to uncover opportunities for service improvements, innovation, and strategic partnership. They should be comfortable leveraging supplier data and performance metrics to surface actionable insights that benefit the organization. Strong stakeholder management is critical—this individual must be able to influence, communicate, and build trust across all levels of the organization while driving alignment and results. The successful candidate will be a proactive problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset, strong operational rigor, and a focus on delivering measurable efficiency gains. Key Responsibilities Operational Excellence & Process Efficiency Drive efficiency and effectiveness across all Procure-to-Pay operations. Ensure seamless integration and connectivity across requisitioning, purchasing, invoicing, and payment processes. Establish and reinforce standardized processes and best practices. Stakeholder Management & Engagement Build and maintain strong relationships with Procurement, AP, Finance, and business stakeholders. Act as a trusted partner and primary point of contact for P2P operational topics. Drive alignment, accountability, and adoption of P2P processes across the organization. Lead stakeholder communication, ensuring clarity and consistency. Training & Educational Activities Develop and deliver training programs to improve user adoption and compliance. Continuously reinforce process adherence through education and engagement Supplier Value Management Identify and capture value from supplier relationships beyond cost—including service quality, innovation, risk mitigation, and strategic partnership opportunities. Develop and maintain supplier scorecards and performance frameworks to drive accountability and continuous improvement. Collaborate with category managers and business owners to maximize the value delivered through supplier engagements. Off-Channel Spend Management Identify, analyze, and address off-contract and off-channel spend. Partner with stakeholders to drive compliance with approved procurement channels. Recommend and implement strategies to improve spend control and visibility. Performance Management (KPIs & Scorecards) Monitor, and report key operational KPIs. Develop and maintain stakeholder and operational scorecards. Design and deliver proactive reporting that surfaces trends, risks, and opportunities before they escalate—enabling leadership to make informed decisions with timely, forward-looking insights. Use data to identify trends, measure performance, and drive continuous improvement. Governance & Compliance Support development and enforcement of procurement policies and controls. Ensure adherence to financial, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements. Assist with audits and ensure proper documentation and process transparency. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Accounting, or related field (or equivalent experience). 5+ years of experience in Procure-to-Pay, Procurement Operations, or Finance Operations. Strong understanding of end-to-end P2P processes and operational workflows. Proven track record of improving operational efficiency and process performance. Demonstrated ability to identify and realize value from supplier relationships across cost, quality, and innovation dimensions. Experience designing and delivering proactive reporting and actionable insights to senior stakeholders. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across all organizational levels. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Experience identifying and addressing off-channel spend is highly preferred. Familiarity with procurement and financial systems (e.g., Coupa, SAP, Ariba, or similar) is a plus. Strengthen stakeholder engagement and process adoption across the organization. Improve spend compliance and visibility through proactive management. Identify and unlock value from supplier relationships to benefit the broader organization. Deliver proactive, insight-driven reporting that keeps leadership ahead of issues and opportunities. Continuous Improvement & Innovation: Identify opportunities for process optimization, tooling improvements, and innovation within the sourcing and procurement function. Experience in the IT category, with a solid understanding of IT cost structures and pricing models. Experience applying a savings methodology and reporting validated savings results. Demonstrated experience building relationships with BU stakeholders and supporting change management for new sourcing strategies and vendors. Strong contract management and negotiation skills. Experience with Coupa or similar procurement/P2P platforms, including intake and approval workflow. Flexible and adaptable, with the ability to shift priorities in a fast-growing environment.
